uncertainty: Sixteen pinned Java Maven package paths passed the valid local HTTP/1.1 GET request control and exposed method, target, Host, and X-Parsarium headers; fifteen also exposed the version. A seventeenth path, Sentinel transport, passed the valid local HTTP/1.1 200 response control and exposed status, Content-Type and body. These are seventeen verified package paths with shared parser ancestry: Netty 3, 4, and 5 share project ancestry, while httpcore and httpcore-nio share the Apache HttpComponents Core 4.x family and httpcore5 is its 5.x branch. Netty 5 is an alpha release and is labeled as such. The working goal of 20 has not been met; three paths remain. Five Maven Central queries were bounded at 100 hits each. The broad http1 and HTTP/1.1 queries each reported 7,858 total and saved the first 100 identical, mostly unrelated HTTP package hits, giving 200 saved hits but only 100 unique; http parser, http request parser, and http codec timed out in the latest snapshot, so they provide no absence evidence. Targeted Maven releases and official API documentation supplied the seventeen verified paths, including NanoHTTPD's documented protected local-stream session API and direct parsers in jwarc, webarchive-commons and JWAT. One plausible lead remains unresolved: a historical WebPieces artifact. Snice codec-http 0.0.12 was excluded after its public classes showed message models but no local raw-message parser API. Other search hits have not all been reviewed, and the most-used top 20 is unknown. Grizzly 5.0.3 adds a native HTTP server codec tested through an in-memory buffer and unconnected filter context. Apache MINA 2.2.10 adds a native server decoder which normalized header names to lowercase in the local control. The pinned release has zero known public direct dependents in deps.dev, so it ranks last. HttpCore NIO 4.4.16 adds a separate Maven artifact and request parser class, but shares HttpComponents lineage with blocking httpcore. The three WARC-oriented packages parse the saved raw HTTP message directly without a WARC container; they expose distinct parser implementations. NanoHTTPD exposes the parsed method, target and headers through a local session callback, but its public session interface does not expose the protocol version; its adapter omits that field. The two ordinary controls establish only the observed request and response subsets; Sentinel requires Content-Length for body parsing and does not support chunked responses. Java SE 25 public APIs reviewed expose network HTTP clients or servers, not a documented local raw message parser. No vulnerability, malformed-input, or resource-use experiments were run.
